observed_architecture_facts.fact: HostPermissionGrant models native permission as a grant with time validity, adapter id and native_permission_ref. resolve_effective_perception_snapshot checks grant validity only at resolution time and derives an effective-host-permission marker from immutable hashes/capabilities/time bounds.

perception_fabric.ObserveIntent.validate_against revalidates exact snapshot digest and is_valid_at(now), but the PerceptionCapabilitySnapshot itself has no native portal/PipeWire session-liveness or revocation state. A same immutable snapshot remains valid until its expiry unless some external component replaces or expires it.

active_sensing_fabric.compile_observe_intent requires the effective-host-permission provenance marker before compilation. This proves host evidence was incorporated at compile time, not that the native permission/session is still alive at later capture time.

WP708 observe_intent.py separately performs exact permission-snapshot revalidation immediately before capture/analysis, but against RetinaPermissionSnapshot. It cannot detect an OS/portal revocation unless that external revocation has first changed the snapshot presented to it.

CaptureOwnerLease binds source id/generation, owner id, open time, source hash and broker-policy hash. It carries no host-grant digest, effective-permission digest or native-session validation digest. acquire_owner therefore proves logical single ownership, not current host authorization.

publish_frame validates active logical owner lease, source generation and monotonic frame ordering. It does not re-check host authorization. The module explicitly delegates actual hardware/native capture to a future local adapter.

perception_fabric.py and observe_intent.py both publish schema identifier FRANKENSTEIN2_OBSERVE_INTENT/v1 for structurally different dataclasses/fields and different permission snapshot models. This is an ABI collision that should be reconciled before treating either path as the single integration authority.

external_constraints_distilled: XDG ScreenCast sessions can close asynchronously and Session.Closed is the native lifecycle signal.
D-Bus creator disappearance closes its sessions.
ScreenCast restore_token is single-use persistence/restore state and is not current liveness proof.
PipeWire/WirePlumber permissions can be dynamically changed/revoked during a client lifetime.
A portal-provided PipeWire remote is a restricted live capability and raw file descriptors are ephemeral process resources, not durable state.

primary_hypothesis.statement: F2 requires a fresh execution-time host-permission witness between immutable planning permission and logical CaptureOwner acquisition. Compile-time host-bound snapshots alone are insufficient for asynchronous native revocation.
primary_hypothesis.reason: Native authorization can change without changing the already-derived immutable F2 snapshot. The capture broker currently has no host-permission binding.

counterhypothesis.statement: A separate execution lease is unnecessary if every host grant has a very short finite TTL and every native revocation synchronously republishes a new current permission snapshot before any capture can proceed.
counterhypothesis.falsifier: Close/revoke a native session after F2 permission compilation but before logical CaptureOwner acquisition while remaining inside the grant TTL. If current F2 validation/acquisition can still succeed without a native liveness read, TTL/snapshot-only semantics are insufficient.

architecture_delta_candidate.name: HOST_PERMISSION_EXECUTION_LEASE
architecture_delta_candidate.placement: host adapter -> execution validation -> CaptureOwner acquisition
invariants: Lease must be produced by a source-specific native adapter after a live permission/session check; arbitrary caller text cannot self-grant it.
Lease must be finite-lived. No indefinite native execution lease for revocable portal/device permissions.
Lease source_id/source_generation must match the source and CaptureOwner generation.
Lease must bind the exact host-grant and effective permission snapshot digests used by planning.
Raw D-Bus object paths, PipeWire file descriptors and other live handles remain process-local; durable receipts store typed digests/identities only where safe and useful.

Session Closed / D-Bus owner loss / terminal native stream error invalidates the lease and forces CaptureOwner release. Reopening/restoring creates a new native execution lease and should advance F2 source generation when the native source instance changes.
Restore tokens never satisfy this lease.
The lease grants sensor execution only to the local capture adapter path; it grants no canonical world fact, GWT fact, effect or completion authority.

capture_broker_binding_delta.preferred: CaptureOwnerLease (or an admitted wrapper replacing it at integration) binds host_permission_execution_lease_sha256 and effective_permission_snapshot_sha256. acquire_owner rejects missing/stale/mismatched execution lease. publish_frame is only valid while that bound native lease is live for capture_monotonic_ns; asynchronous revocation releases owner and prevents new frame refs.
capture_broker_binding_delta.why: The broker is the single-owner choke point. Binding permission freshness here prevents every downstream consumer from inventing its own native permission semantics while keeping the OS adapter outside canonical world/effect authority.

observe_intent_abi_reconciliation.recommended_resolution: Before host integration, choose one canonical v2 ObserveIntent contract or explicitly rename/version the WP708 Retina-specific contract. The admitted execution path should have one exact current permission digest and one native execution-lease binding, not two same-version ABIs.
observe_intent_abi_reconciliation.nonclaim: This E2 does not select or implement the final migration because Trigger4 owns product build/integration.

source_specific_adapter_notes.SCREENCAST_DISPLAY_WINDOW: Use portal Session lifecycle; session closure is revocation/liveness input. Preserve portal stream id as logical mapping aid, and use PipeWire object.serial/pipewire-serial rather than reusable node id for a native stream instance when available.
source_specific_adapter_notes.CAMERA: Use Camera AccessCamera/OpenPipeWireRemote permission semantics. Do not fabricate a ScreenCast Session when the native Camera portal contract is different; map both to the common F2 execution-lease ABI through source-specific adapters.
source_specific_adapter_notes.BROWSER_RENDERED_OR_STRUCTURAL: Use the browser's native permission/lifecycle semantics; do not inherit XDG details unless the actual host path uses them.

trigger4_handoff_acceptance_tests: T1_COMPILE_THEN_NATIVE_REVOKE: compile/admit with valid host evidence, signal native revoke before owner acquisition, require acquisition failure.
T2_REVOKE_AFTER_OWNER_ACQUIRE: revoke/close native session after owner acquisition, require owner release/invalidation and reject subsequent publish_frame; frame count must not advance.
T3_REOPEN_RESTORE: restored/reopened source cannot reuse prior execution lease; new session/source instance gets a new lease and appropriate source generation.
T4_RESTORE_TOKEN_NEGATIVE: possession of restore token alone cannot create execution lease.
T5_ARBITRARY_NATIVE_REF_NEGATIVE: caller-supplied native_permission_ref without adapter validation cannot create execution lease.
T6_ABI_COLLISION: incompatible ObserveIntent structures cannot both serialize as the same schema/version in admitted integration.
T7_BOUNDARY: no permission/session receipt grants world-truth, EffectGate bypass, completion or model-output authority.
next_high_information_discriminator: E3 deterministic stale-revocation fixture against exact current source: derive an effective host-bound snapshot, compile/validate it, model native session closure without changing the immutable snapshot, then demonstrate that current F2 source-level checks cannot observe the closure and logical CaptureOwner acquisition remains possible. This is a source-level falsifier only, not native runtime evidence.
